title: Regulating More Than Teaching: Generative Artificial Intelligence in the Course Syllabi of a Brazilian University
content: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) has rapidly reached higher education, but little is known about how institutions translate it into everyday course planning. This study examines how GenAI appears in the undergraduate course syllabi of a Brazilian community university. In a census-based documentary study, all 2851 syllabi from the first semester of 2026 were manually coded with 20 binary indicators across five dimensions (AI presence, pedagogical uses, assessment, critical education, and the role of AI in teaching), and textual statements on AI were classified by tone. Proportions were estimated with Beta-Binomial models, and associations were assessed with Bayes factors. GenAI was addressed in 13.1% of syllabi (95% CrI: 11.9–14.4), mainly as a rule on assessment and authorship; AI literacy and social impacts of AI appeared in two syllabi or fewer. Variation was structured by school, not by campus, shift, or course type. The 375 statements on AI corresponded to only 166 distinct texts, and two templates accounted for 38.7% of them. GenAI thus enters course planning mainly as a replicated clause regulating student conduct, not as an object of teaching. Institutions should revise these templates and help faculty turn rules into pedagogical guidance.
